Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT A. Francisco Gold Condominium II Bldg., cor EDSA Mapagmahal Street, Diliman, Quezon City LEGAL SLRVICE DILG OPINION NO. 154 S. 2010 24 November 2010 MR. RICARTE A. NAGAC Chairman, SVHAI No. 17 Lotus St., Sampaguita Village San Pedro, Laguna Dear Mr. Nagac: This pertains to your letter dated 07 September 2010 where you protested as illegal and violative of PD 1216 the barangay-sponsored construction of a multi-purpose hall and garage for barangay vehicles. Section 2 of PD 1216 provides, thus: "SECTION 2. Section 31 of Presidential Decree No. 957 is hereby amended to read as follows: SECTION 31. Roads, Alleys, Sidewalks and Open Spaces.- The owner as developer of a subdivision shall provide adequate roads, alleys and sidewalks. xxx xxx xxx These areas reserved for parks, playgrounds and recreational use shall be non-alienable public lands, and non-buildable. The plans of the subdivision projects shall include three planting on such parks of the subdivision as may be designated by the Authority. Upon their completion as certified to by the Authority, the roads, alleys, sidewalks and playgrounds shall be donated by the owner or developer to the city or municipality and it shall be mandatory for the local governments to accept provided, however, that the parks and playgrounds may be donated to the Homeowners Association of the project with the consent of the city or municipality concerned. No portion of the parks and playgrounds donated thereafter shall be converted to any other purpose or purposes." A reading of the foregoing provision easily yields that there are two sets of proscriptions, to wit: 1. That the area reserved for parks, playgrounds and recreational use shall be inalienable and non-buildable; and 2. That the donated properties or any portion thereof shall not be converted for any other purpose or purposes.

-2- While it is not expressly provided for in the provision, the first proscription pertains to the owner-developer of the subdivision, while the second proscription refers to the donee of these roads, alleys, sidewalks and playground, which can either be the city or municipality or the homeowners association, strictly in that order of preference. To resolve the issue which you belabored in your letter, it is imperative to establish the ownership of the playground where these constructions are made as once established, we can determine the validity or invalidity of the subject construction. Thus, if the ownership of the playground is with the developer or the homeowners association, the subject construction undertaken by the barangay is illegal as it contravenes Section 305 (b) of RA 7160 (Local Government Code), which provides: "SEC. 305. Fundamental Principles.- The financial affairs, transactions, and operations of local government units shall be governed by the following fundamental principles: xxx (b) Local government funds and monies shall be spend solely for public purposes." On the other hand, if the ownership of the playground is vested with the barangay through any of the means which can convey ownership, such as but not limited to, donations, then the construction is perforce legal and valid as the act of construction is nothing more than an incident of ownership. The prohibitions under PD 1216, namely: the non-conversion of the donated property or any part thereof to other purposes or the "non- buildable clause" do not apply as they are made applicable only to the developer, homeowners associations or the city/municipality, excluding the barangay under the principle "inclusion unius est exclusion alterius" (what the law does not include, it excludes). One of the attributes of a local government unit, such as a barangay, is to acquire and convey real and personal property (Sec. 22, RA 7160). In your 07 September 2010 letter, it is unclear whether the playground had been donated to the barangay. You can, however, easily determine this fact from your end and conclude accordingly per the guidelines enumerated in this letter-opinion. We hope to have enlightened you on the matter. Very truly yours, ATTY. ESUS B. DOQUE 1 Director Ill
